summary: Experts warn that renewed military confrontation between Cambodia and Thailand during the global energy crisis would be devastating. Following intense clashes involving airstrikes and artillery in late 2025, a fragile ceasefire is currently in place. However, Thailand’s army intelligence chief recently accused Cambodia of preparing for a 'third round' of war, prompting calls for Thai forces to remain on high alert. Analysts emphasize that Cambodia may hold strategic advantages in certain border areas despite Thailand's overall power projection capabilities.
title: Border clash amid Mideast crisis will hurt region, say experts

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona issued a statement on April 1, 2026, regarding the situation at the Cambodia-Thailand border. He stated that the government remains committed to protecting the nation's territory and people, while praising citizens for their active role in territorial defense and supporting displaced compatriots. Bona emphasized that Cambodia's firm stance is to resolve issues peacefully through mature diplomacy and patience to avoid military confrontation and tension.
title: Government Spokesman: The Royal Government Never Forgets the Duty to 'Protect Territorial Integrity'

summary: Ambassador-designate Chum Sounry met with Japanese officials in Tokyo to discuss the current situation on the Cambodia-Thailand border. He reiterated Cambodia's commitment to a peaceful resolution through existing bilateral mechanisms like the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC). Sounry thanked Japan for its understanding and humanitarian support provided to Cambodian civilians affected by the border conflict.
title: Cambodia’s ambassador-designate to Japan strengthens ties with Tokyo

summary: Political expert Dr. Seun Sam argues that Cambodia must strengthen ties with France to protect its sovereignty against the territorial ambitions of neighbors like Thailand. He highlights the historical role of France in protecting Cambodia since 1863 and emphasizes that France's technical assistance with historical maps and border documents is essential for resolving current disputes.
title: Dr. Seun Sam: Cambodia should strengthen relations with France

summary: Major General Hul Sam On, Commander of Transport Brigade 99, visited Cambodian soldiers stationed along the Thai-Cambodian border to provide encouragement and supplies ahead of the Khmer New Year. He praised the troops' sacrifices in defending national peace despite being away from their families. The visit included the distribution of food, money, and essential materials to boost morale on the frontline.
title: Major General Hul Sam On visits troops stationed along the Cambodia-Thailand border for Khmer New Year

source: Asia News Network / Phnom Penh Post
summary: Chinese Ambassador Wang Wenbin met with National Assembly President Khuon Sudary, pledging that Beijing will not abandon Cambodia regarding security and defense. China intends to act as a 'bridge for peace' to help restore normalcy in Cambodia-Thailand relations. Additionally, a '2+2' strategic dialogue involving foreign and defense ministers from both China and Cambodia is scheduled to take place soon to strengthen military ties.
title: China stands with Cambodia on defence, vows Chinese FM Wang Yi

summary: Acting Head of State Hun Sen reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to a durable ceasefire and peaceful resolution of border issues through bilateral mechanisms. During a meeting with the Singaporean Ambassador, he thanked Singapore for providing observers to monitor the border situation and emphasized the importance of high-level diplomacy to maintain stability.
title: Samdech Techo Hun Sen: Cambodia Committed to Long-term Ceasefire

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence has rejected Thai claims of 'provocative actions' at the O'Smach border. Spokeswoman Lt Gen Maly Socheata stated that Thai forces deployed two armored vehicles and 70 personnel to the area on April 2 without notice. Cambodia has officially contacted Thai Army Region 2 to demand an immediate halt to these military movements, asserting that Cambodian troops are following strict orders to maintain peace while safeguarding sovereignty.
title: Cambodia urges Thailand to respect ceasefire and maintain border stability

summary: Incoming Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul plans to cancel the 2001 MOU 44 on overlapping maritime and land claims as a key policy shift. The move, expected to be finalized after the new Cabinet takes office on April 6, 2026, threatens to reopen sensitive disputes over undersea resources and land control. The Thai military insists that any resource sharing must be linked to maritime boundary demarcation, a point of long-standing friction with Cambodian leadership.
title: Thailand to tear up MOU 44 as Hun Sen blocks border reset

summary: Battambang Governor Sok Lou visited Cambodian soldiers stationed along the Thailand-Cambodia border to offer encouragement and supplies. The visit aims to boost morale for troops protecting the border during the upcoming Khmer New Year celebrations.
title: Battambang governor meets frontline forces, delivers support ahead of Khmer New Year

summary: Reports indicate that the Thai government intends to include the cancellation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia into its official policy statement. This move follows ongoing internal Thai political pressure regarding territorial integrity.
title: Thailand to include cancellation of maritime MoU with Cambodia in policy statement

summary: Cambodian media reports accuse Thailand of using media narratives and international diplomatic visits (such as to Paris) to justify its encroachment on Cambodian territory. Prime Minister Hun Manet has previously claimed Thai forces are occupying Cambodian soil using shipping containers and barbed wire, calling for the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to verify facts using 1904-1907 historical maps.
title: Thailand's 'diplomatic manipulation' of border dispute criticized by Cambodia

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has established a 'hunting unit' to stop fuel smuggling into Cambodia, labeling the smugglers 'evil' and 'national traitors.' The crackdown follows reports from the Royal Thai Navy of a major cross-border operation that is allegedly siphoning Thai resources and inflating local prices.
title: Thai PM Anutin labels oil smugglers to Cambodia as 'national traitors'

summary: General Vong Pisen, Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces, praised the ASEAN Observation Team (AOT) for their role in monitoring the border. During a ceremony on April 2, he thanked Malaysia for its support in the ceasefire implementation. He noted that while the situation is stabilizing, observers have had to work under difficult conditions, including the threat of gunfire from the other side. He emphasized that Cambodia remains committed to international law and existing mechanisms to resolve the dispute.
title: Commander-in-Chief reaffirms Cambodia's stance on peaceful border resolution with Thailand

summary: Acting Head of State Hun Sen reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to a durable ceasefire and peaceful negotiations during a meeting with the new Singaporean Ambassador. He emphasized that border disputes with Thailand must be handled through existing bilateral mechanisms and dialogue rather than confrontation. He also expressed appreciation for Singapore’s role in monitoring the border situation through observers.
title: Resolving Cambodia–Thailand border issues require a lasting ceasefire and peaceful negotiations, Acting Head of State says

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has ordered a high-level investigation into reports of fuel being smuggled from Thailand into Cambodia. He warned that any private companies involved will lose their business licenses, and any government officials or military personnel found complicit will be immediately fired and expelled from the state framework. This comes after Cambodia officially banned fuel imports from Thailand in June 2025, claiming they have enough supply from other partners.
title: PM orders probe into alleged illegal fuel smuggling from Thailand, warns of license revocation and dismissals

summary: Senate President Hun Sen reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to a lasting ceasefire and peaceful negotiations with Thailand. The Ministry of Interior reported that over 94% of the 640,000 displaced people have returned home, though over 34,900 remain in camps as of April 2. In border provinces like Oddar Meanchey and Preah Vihear, several schools and health facilities remain closed due to security concerns. Officials noted that Thailand has not fully complied with border committee statements, and Cambodian authorities continue to document alleged violations.
title: Cambodia pursues peaceful border solution, boosts aid to displaced

summary: The Ministry of National Defence officially rejected claims that its forces were escalating tensions. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata stated that while an ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) verified the calm at O'Smach on March 29, Thai forces subsequently deployed armored vehicles and 70 personnel on April 2. Cambodia claims the Thai side reinforced barbed wire without notifying the Military Region 4 Liaison Team, violating the de-escalation measures agreed upon in late 2025.
title: Cambodia Urges Thailand to Respect Ceasefire and Maintain Border Stability

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that Cambodia is pursuing "active diplomacy" regarding the Thai border situation. Acting Head of State Hun Sen met with the Singaporean Ambassador to discuss ASEAN observers monitoring the border. Simultaneously, PM Hun Manet has ordered a strict crackdown on illegal fuel smuggling from Thailand, reminding officials that all fuel imports from Thailand have been officially suspended since June 2025.
title: Cambodia Intensifies Global Diplomacy Amid Border Strains and PM's France Visit

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence reported that Thai forces illegally deployed two armored vehicles and 70 personnel to the O'Smach International Border Crossing in Oddar Meanchey on April 2. Cambodian officials rejected Thai social media claims of provocation, stating their troops are acting with restraint while guarding sovereignty. Cambodia called on Thailand to respect a 2025 peace agreement and stop unauthorized activities.
title: Thai military deploys armored vehicles, troops to O'Smach crossing, Cambodia rejects claims

summary: Senate President Hun Sen reaffirmed Cambodia's stance on solving the border dispute with Thailand peacefully during a meeting with the newly appointed Singaporean ambassador. He emphasized that the government remains committed to the 2025 ceasefire agreement. Simultaneously, RCAF Commander-in-Chief Vong Pisen praised the role of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) in monitoring border security and maintaining transparency.
title: Senate president reiterates Kingdom's commitment to peaceful negotiations, ceasefire

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of April 2, 79 more people displaced by the border conflict have returned home. Currently, 34,939 people (including over 18,000 women and 11,000 children) remain in camps. Schools and health centers in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Preah Vihear provinces stay closed, though no new property damage has been reported since late 2025.
title: Over 34,000 people remain in displacement camps

summary: Reports indicate an increase in arrests of Cambodian citizens speaking out about border issues. This comes at a time when the Cambodian government is officially accusing the Thai military of reinforcing barbed wire and deploying armored vehicles in the O'Smach area, which Cambodia considers occupied territory.
title: ការចាប់ខ្លួនអ្នកនិយាយបញ្ហាព្រំដែនមានសន្ទុះកើនឡើងទោះរដ្ឋាភិបាលថាថៃឈ្លានពានអត់ឈប់

summary: Cambodia lodged a formal protest regarding incidents between March 31 and April 2, 2026, involving Thai forces in Banteay Meanchey and Oddar Meanchey provinces. Reports indicate Thai personnel conducted land-ownership verifications and installed barbed wire at the O'Smach International Border Gate. Cambodia views these moves as attempts to create a 'fait accompli' before official demarcation is finished. The government reiterated its commitment to peaceful resolution but insisted borders must not be changed by force.
title: Cambodia Protests Unlawful Thai Actions in Border Areas

summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Sok Chenda Sophea issued a formal protest late yesterday regarding Thai military actions between March 31 and April 2. The ministry reports that Thai 'Burapha' forces led citizens to verify land ownership near pillars 45 and 47 in Banteay Meanchey, which Cambodia calls an attempt to create a 'fait accompli.' Further tensions were noted on April 2 when 70 Thai soldiers and two armored vehicles deployed at the O'Smach gate to install barbed wire, while heavy machinery cleared land in Anlong Veng. Cambodia demands a withdrawal to restore the status quo.
title: Cambodia lodges formal protest against Thai border incursions

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs protested Thai activities involving land verification along the border in Chouk Chey village, Banteay Meanchey. The ministry stated it absolutely does not recognize any unilateral boundary lines or territorial claims made by Thailand. The report highlights that on April 2, 2026, about 70 Thai soldiers with two armored vehicles deployed additional barbed wire at the O'Smach International Border Gate and cleared land near a border pillar in Anlong Veng district, Oddar Meanchey.
title: Cambodia says Thailand illegally attempts to establish 'de facto' land occupation

summary: Cambodian officials have dismissed reports in Thai media alleging that members of the Cambodian Bodyguard Headquarters (BHQ) infiltrated Thailand for espionage and sabotage. The government labeled these claims as "false and baseless." Simultaneously, National Defence Minister General Tea Seiha visited frontline troops in Military Region 5 (Banteay Meanchey and Battambang) to boost morale ahead of the Khmer New Year, thanking them for protecting national sovereignty.
title: Cambodia debunks 'false' espionage claims of Thai media

summary: Geopolitical expert Dr. Nyil Ratha claims the Thai government under Anutin is using 'fascist-style' tactics to distract from internal crises. He argues that settling Thai farmers on disputed land near Prey Chan and Chouk Chey villages is a strategy to create 'human shields' and fake evidence of Thai residency for international courts, while also pressuring Cambodia in maritime energy negotiations.
title: Dr. Nyil Ratha: Anutin is playing a dangerous game for neighbors

summary: The Cambodian government issued a formal protest following incidents on April 4, 2026, near the Preah Vihear Temple. Cambodian authorities reported that Thai troops performed land-clearing, installed 100 meters of barbed wire, and deployed armored vehicles in the Bosbov-Choam Tae area. Cambodia claims these actions violate sovereignty under the 1904/1907 treaties and rejected what it calls an attempt to create a 'fait accompli' on the ground.
title: Cambodia Strongly Protests Thailand's Unlawful and Repeated Activities in Illegally Occupied Border Areas

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that while 92% of displaced civilians have returned since the December 2025 ceasefire, 49,331 people remain displaced. The government cited continued 'dishonest activities' by the Thai military, including the placement of shipping containers and encroachment on territory, as the primary reason these citizens cannot yet safely return to their border villages.
title: Ministry of Interior: Over 49,000 displaced people unable to return home

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest against Thai armed forces for land-clearing activities on April 4, 2026, near Preah Vihear Temple. Cambodia claims Thai troops laid 100 meters of barbed wire and deployed armored vehicles in the Bosbov-Choam Tae area. The statement rejects any 'fait accompli' attempts by Thailand to occupy land and demands an immediate halt to these unilateral actions.
title: Cambodia protests 'illegal activities' by Thai forces at Choam Ksan near Preah Vihear

summary: The Cambodian government has lodged a formal protest against Thailand, accusing Thai armed forces of "unlawful and repeated activities" in disputed areas near Preah Vihear province. Specifically, Cambodia claims Thai troops performed land-clearing operations and laid 100 meters of barbed wire near the Preah Vihear Temple on Saturday. Additionally, Cambodia rejected Thai allegations of provocation at the O'Smach International Border Checkpoint, stating that Thai forces reinforced barbed wire there without notification. Over 610,000 displaced persons have reportedly returned home, though 34,000 remain in camps.
title: Cambodia protests Thai activities in disputed border areas

summary: Recent economic reports indicate that the border conflict with Thailand could drop Cambodia's GDP growth below 4% in 2026 if tensions escalate further. The closure of six major border crossings has already disrupted trade, particularly in fuel and petroleum where Cambodia relies on Thailand for 30% of its imports. Tourism has also suffered, with Thai visitors—previously 30% of international arrivals—plummeting due to stricter border controls and negative sentiment.
title: Economic Shockwaves from Cambodia–Thailand Border Conflict Threaten 2026 Growth

summary: Senate Second Vice-President Thun Vathana stated that international law is the primary mechanism for resolving the border dispute with Thailand. Despite public anxiety over territorial loss, he reassured citizens that the border remains calm and that diplomats are monitoring the situation. He noted that Cambodia referred disputes to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in June 2025 following previous armed clashes. Vathana expressed hope that a new Thai government, to be formed after recent elections, would return to peaceful negotiations.
title: Int'l law key to resolving spat with Thailand, says Vathana

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona reported that front-line soldiers and civilians displaced by border tensions are receiving support and 'warmth' from Cambodia's top national leaders. This comes as military personnel remain stationed along the border following recent reports of Thai military activities in contested zones near Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey.
title: Heroes of the army and displaced civilians receive warmth from leadership

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated during a press conference on April 6 that Cambodia strongly rejects Thai attempts to create a 'fait accompli' on the ground. He cited Thai military activity on April 4 near the Keo Sikha Kiri Svara Pagoda involving land clearing and armored vehicle deployment. The spokesperson emphasized that Cambodia does not recognize unilateral Thai border claims and demands a return to the status quo defined by the 1904 and 1907 treaties.
title: Cambodia protests again against Thai military aggression

summary: Official state news reports that Cambodia sent a diplomatic note to Thailand proposing a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap between April 17-22. Cambodia wants to deploy joint survey teams to place markers in disputed areas of Banteay Meanchey and Battambang. The statement also warns against Thai military occupying what Cambodia claims is its territory.
title: Cambodia Urges Thailand to Hold Urgent Border Talks and Resume Demarcation Work

summary: The Cambodian Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) sent a diplomatic note to Thailand on April 7, 2026, requesting an urgent meeting between April 17 and 22 in Siem Reap. The request aims to resume field surveys and temporary border marking at several points including O'Chrov district (Banteay Meanchey) and Kamrieng district (Battambang). Cambodia noted that Thailand has repeatedly postponed meetings citing internal cabinet appointments.
title: Cambodia again requests Thailand to organize urgent special JBC meeting in April

summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Tea Seiha visited soldiers stationed at the frontlines along the Cambodia-Thailand border in Koh Kong and Preah Sihanouk provinces. During the visit, he delivered New Year greetings and praised the troops for their mission in defending Cambodia's territorial integrity and sovereignty ahead of the upcoming Khmer New Year celebrations.
title: Deputy PM Tea Seiha visits troops on frontline along Cambodia-Thailand border for New Year

summary: The State Secretariat of Border Affairs has sent a formal request (Note Verbale) to Thailand to urgently convene a Joint Border Commission (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap between April 17 and 22, 2026. Cambodia wants to resume technical work and place temporary markers in disputed areas of Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, and Oddar Meanchey. This move follows Cambodian complaints about 'unlawful' activities by Thai troops who have allegedly occupied areas in Preah Vihear province.
title: Cambodia Proposes Special JBC Meeting with Thailand to Resume Border Work

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that border developments are the primary focus of diplomatic talks in Phnom Penh. Cambodia officially rejected unilateral territorial claims by Thailand and reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution via international law. Bona noted that Senate President Hun Sen is pushing for a lasting ceasefire and dialogue through existing bilateral channels. The government also expressed support for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to monitor the border.
title: Cambodia denies Thailand's territorial claims

summary: Thai military officials conducted a media tour of the O'Smach Resort complex, a massive scam center covering 80 hectares that they seized in December during the border conflict. Thailand claims the area was being used as a base for launching attacks against their forces. The complex, linked to sanctioned politician Ly Yong Phat, highlights the intersection of organized crime and border instability. While Thai forces occupy the facility, the Cambodian government continues to protest the military presence in the area.
title: Inside a Huge Compound on Thailand-Cambodia Border Where 10,000 Workers Scammed People Globally

summary: A Cambodian official has rejected Thailand's attempts to justify its military actions through organized media and military attaché visits to the O’Smach area in Oddar Meanchey province. Cambodia claims the Thai army is illegally occupying territory and using the pretext of fighting online scams to justify territorial encroachment. The official also dismissed Thai allegations about Cambodian military activity as 'baseless' and part of a disinformation narrative.
title: Cambodia denounces repeated Thai illegal activities, rejects military claims

summary: The Cambodian State Secretariat of Border Affairs has sent a Note Verbale to Thailand proposing a special Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap between April 17 and 22, 2026. Cambodia is pushing to resume field surveys and the placement of temporary markers in disputed areas including Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, and O’Smach. The statement reaffirms Cambodia's stance against the illegal occupation of its territory by Thai forces.
title: Cambodia urges Thailand to hold urgent border talks and resume demarcation work

summary: Cambodia has reaffirmed its position regarding the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on maritime boundaries. This follows reports that the Thai government under Anutin Charnvirakul might consider withdrawing from the framework. Cambodian officials warn that such a move would damage bilateral cooperation and ignore established mechanisms for resolving overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand.
title: Cambodia warns Thai withdrawal from MOU-2001 would undermine cooperation spirit

summary: The National Authority for Preah Vihear (NAPV) reports that the 11th-century temple sustained significant damage from heavy artillery and airstrikes during military aggression last year. Experts identified 562 damage points, estimating that stabilization alone will take 5 to 10 years, while full restoration could take 30 years and cost tens of millions of dollars. Unexploded ordnance remains a major obstacle to beginning the work.
title: It will take up to three decades to undo the damage inflicted on Preah Vihear Temple by Thai forces

summary: Civil society and political activists are urging the Hun Manet government to station actual troops at the border to prevent Thai soldiers from encroaching on Cambodian soil. The report mentions that Thailand has ignored over 700 protest letters from Cambodia. Activists suggest filing an immediate complaint against Thailand instead of relying on ignored diplomacy, noting that Thai troops remain at over 50 locations on Cambodian territory.
title: Cambodia should prevent Thailand from actually invading its territory, rather than issuing a letter that Thailand ignores

summary: Minister Delegate Jean-François Tain stated that reclaiming land illegally held by the Thai military is a top government priority. Following PM Hun Manet's return from France, Tain emphasized that Cambodia must think strategically to recover territory occupied since the December ceasefire. He cited a recent April 2 incident where Thai forces moved armored vehicles and 70 troops into the O'Smach international border area in Oddar Meanchey to install more barbed wire without prior notice.
title: Jean-François Tain: Cambodia Demands Return of Land Occupied by Thai Military

summary: Phnom Penh has officially requested a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting to resume land demarcation following 'unlawful' activities by Thai armed forces in disputed areas. The Cambodian side of the JBC submitted a note verbale on April 7, proposing a six-point plan to restart stalled work. This includes dispatching joint survey teams to Banteay Meanchey and Battambang provinces between April 20 and 24. Cambodia alleges that Thai troops are illegally occupying territory in four provinces—Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat—and have used shipping containers to block villagers from returning home.
title: Cambodia calls for urgent JBC talks with Thailand over illegal border occupation

summary: CCTV footage has circulated showing unidentified men smuggling boxes of cigarettes into Thailand through Doung village in Battambang province. Local analysts warn that such illegal activities undermine national dignity and public trust, especially during current border tensions. Critics point to potential lapses in authority oversight at the border during this sensitive period.
title: Social media images expose cross-border smuggling of contraband

summary: In a video update, the Royal Government of Cambodia reiterated that regaining territory occupied by Thailand remains its 'top priority.' The government urges citizens not to be swayed by foreign propaganda and explains that it is now carefully choosing the best 'strategic approach' to pursue these claims. The messaging focuses on long-term vision and national sovereignty after reaching a turning point in the recent conflict.
title: VIDEO: Government adopts strategic approach to border dispute

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed concern over reports that the new Thai government may withdraw from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims. Cambodia argues the pact is essential for sharing oil and gas resources in the disputed sea zone. Officials stated that a sudden withdrawal would be regrettable and counter-productive to over 20 years of cooperation. This reaction follows pledges from Thai politicians to cancel the deal to protect Thai interests.
title: Cambodia defends maritime pact as Thailand weighs withdrawal

summary: During his visit to France, Prime Minister Hun Manet briefed President Emmanuel Macron on the border situation, describing Thai actions as aggressive. However, he clarified that Cambodia wants international support for a peaceful legal resolution rather than asking foreign powers to intervene or take sides in the dispute.
title: Manet informs Macron of Thai aggression, does not ask France to 'take sides'

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a warning against Thailand's reported plan to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims. Cambodia argues that unilateral withdrawal violates international law and the spirit of cooperation. The statement emphasizes that the agreement, which involves a 50-50 profit-sharing model for oil and gas, should remain in force until its objectives are achieved, and that domestic Thai laws cannot be used to justify revoking a bilateral treaty.
title: Cambodia warns Thailand against scrapping maritime MoU

summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) warned on April 10 that Cambodia's 4.5% growth projection for 2026 is at risk due to border disruptions with Thailand, rising trade barriers, and global oil shocks. Border tensions are specifically cited as a threat to trade, tourism, and remittance inflows.
title: Growth outlook under threat as three major shocks weigh on economy: ADB

summary: The Ministry of Interior reports that 34,867 Cambodians remain displaced and unable to return to their homes as of April 9, despite a ceasefire that began in late 2025. While over 610,000 people have returned home, those remaining in shelters are blocked by Thai forces using barbed wire and shipping containers. Essential services like schools and hospitals in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Preah Vihear remain closed due to the presence of Thai troops in areas Cambodia claims as its own territory.
title: Nearly 35,000 remain displaced amid ongoing border tensions: Interior Ministry

summary: The Cambodian Foreign Ministry has issued a formal protest against what it calls illegal activities by Thai forces in Battambang and Oddar Meanchey provinces. The government claims these actions violate Cambodia's sovereignty and the current ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia Protests Thailand's Unlawful Actions in Border Areas

summary: During a groundbreaking ceremony for the Funan Techo Project on April 11, Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Cambodia is not asking the world to take sides in the border conflict with Thailand, but rather to uphold international law and the UN Charter. He emphasized that bilateral talks are the fastest way to resolve the dispute and mentioned that both countries remain committed to the December 27, 2025, Joint Statement to maintain current troop positions and avoid new movements.
title: PM: Cambodia Seeks International Support for Truth and Justice, Not Sides

summary: An opinion piece argues that Thai military presence and infrastructure development near the O'Smach area represent an encroachment on Cambodian sovereignty. It claims Thailand is using diplomatic talk as a pretext while strengthening its military grip on contested grounds.
title: Pretexts and Power Plays: Why the World Should Scrutinise Thailand’s Actions on Cambodian Territory

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) issued a formal protest against Thai armed forces for 'unlawful activities' in Battambang and Oddar Meanchey. Specific incidents cited include the planting of a Thai flag at O'Smach on April 6, the construction of unauthorized fences since April 2, and a Thai media visit to the Royal Hill Hotel on April 7 led by a Thai Air Chief Marshal. Cambodia claims these actions violate its sovereignty and the December 2025 de-escalation agreement.
title: Cambodia protests Thai military activity at border

summary: During a ceremony in Takeo province, PM Hun Manet stated that Thailand is currently reorganizing its Joint Border Commission (JBC) to facilitate negotiations. He emphasized that armed conflict is not a sustainable solution and that Cambodia remains committed to peaceful, rules-based settlement. However, reports mention ongoing issues, including a shipping-container barricade erected by Thai forces and displacement camps holding over 34,000 people due to previous clashes.
title: Thailand to refine JBC mechanism amid push to resolve border disputes

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet expressed hope on April 11 that the ongoing border issues with Thailand would be settled quickly to ensure peace and safety for citizens living on both sides of the border. The Premier's remarks come amid recent diplomatic efforts to stabilize the frontier following previous escalations.
title: Samdech Thipadei hopes Cambodia-Thailand border dispute can be resolved soon

summary: In a series of statements, PM Hun Manet reaffirmed that Cambodia is seeking justice, not just taking sides, regarding the border dispute. He expressed hope that the Joint Border Statement from December 27, 2025, remains the path to a permanent resolution. He also praised local authorities for helping families displaced by the ongoing tensions.
title: PM Hun Manet Hopes Thailand Will Uphold Joint Border Agreement

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has called on Thailand to honor the border agreements from the December 2025 ceasefire. He emphasized Point 3 of the agreement, which states that temporary setups don't change the actual border. He wants the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to start surveying and clearing mines in disputed areas immediately so civilians can live safely.
title: Cambodia urges swift implementation of border demarcation agreement with Thailand

summary: Cambodia has urged Thailand to resume border talks following deadly clashes last year that displaced over a million people. PM Hun Manet stated Cambodia is 'fully ready' for talks to ensure peace for border residents. However, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow countered that Thailand is not yet ready due to its own internal 'procedures.' Cambodia also claims Thai forces are currently occupying areas in violation of the December ceasefire and has demanded their withdrawal.
title: Cambodia pushes for renewed border dialogue as Thailand cites procedural hurdles

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has urged the prompt implementation of the Joint Border Commission (JBC) mechanisms following the December 2025 ceasefire. He emphasized that both sides need to resume joint survey and demarcation work, especially in areas where civilians reside. Cambodia remains committed to the December 27, 2025, Joint Statement to ensure long-term peace and security from landmines for survey teams.
title: Cambodia urges swift implementation of border agreement with Thailand

summary: A UN report highlights a 'double shock' to Cambodia caused by the 2025 border conflict, including the displacement of 644,000 people and the return of 900,000 migrant workers. Remittances are projected to drop by $942 million through 2026, leading to fears of landlessness and debt as families lose their primary income source.
title: UN warns displacement, remittance losses, could trigger economic crash in border communities

summary: The Ministry of Labor and Vocational Training announced that as of April 10, 2026, there are 91,234 job vacancies across Cambodia waiting for former migrant workers returning from Thailand. This push comes as many workers return for the Khmer New Year amidst border tensions. The government is encouraging these workers to find employment within the country in sectors like agriculture and industry rather than returning to Thailand.
title: Ministry of Labor: Over 90,000 jobs available for returning workers from Thailand

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that he will not allow foreign entities to destroy the nation, specifically addressing the ongoing border situation where he alleges Thailand has continued 'invasions' for over six months. The rhetoric emphasizes national protection and sovereignty in the face of persistent border friction.
title: Hun Manet says he will not let foreigners destroy Cambodia even though Thailand continues to invade for more than half a year

summary: The Royal Thai Navy stated on April 14 that they have not yet received a formal request from the Cambodian government to reopen border checkpoints in Chanthaburi and Trat. While informal talks have occurred at the local level, the Navy emphasizes that any decision depends on national security and must follow official channels. This follows the December 2025 ceasefire which ended 20 days of intense fighting that killed over 100 people and displaced half a million.
title: Thai Navy says Cambodia has made no formal border request

source: Asia News Network / Phnom Penh Post
summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet announced a shift in strategy regarding the border dispute with Thailand, moving away from international litigation at the ICJ toward direct bilateral negotiations. During a ceremony on April 11, he noted that international courts take too long, leaving border residents in 'perpetual uncertainty.' He welcomed Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul’s recent policy to resolve disputes peacefully and stated that both governments are now 'aligned' in their approach. The two nations continue to follow the December 27 Joint Statement to keep troop positions stable.
title: Cambodia shifts border resolution priorities: ‘From ICJ to bilateral negotiations’

summary: Local media reports a surge in arrests of activists and citizens speaking out about the border dispute. While the government claims Thailand has encroached on Cambodian territory in dozens of locations since the ceasefire three months ago, authorities are reportedly pressuring victims not to reveal details to the public, leading to criticism of the administration's 'soft' response compared to internal crackdowns.
title: Arrests of border activists increase despite government claims of continuous Thai incursions

summary: A new UN report highlights a 'double shock' from the late 2025 border conflict, with 644,000 people displaced and 900,000 migrant workers returning to Cambodia. Remittances are projected to drop by $665 million in 2026, threatening families with landlessness as they struggle to pay microfinance debts. The conflict also closed 883 schools and 50 health facilities, severely disrupting local lives and development gains.
title: UN warns displacement could trigger economic crash in Thai-Cambodia border communities

summary: Following the closure of several border points due to the ongoing conflict, experts in Cambodia are labeling the continued smuggling of goods across the Thai-Cambodian border as an 'act of treason.' They are urging the Royal Government to investigate and take strict legal action against any corrupt officials who may be facilitating this illegal trade while official crossings remain restricted or shut for security reasons.
title: Experts call for probe into officials over illegal border trade

summary: A spokesperson for the Cambodian Senate strongly denied rumors from Thai social media claiming that Senate President Hun Sen admitted fault over a leaked audio recording and secretly attempted to restore relations with Thailand. The spokesperson labeled the claims as fake news created by Thai extremist groups and urged the public to verify information before sharing.
title: Senate spokesperson rejects claims on Thai social media about Hun Sen restoring ties

summary: The Ministry of National Defence has officially denied reports from Thai media and social media claiming Cambodia requested the reopening of the border for emergency goods. Spokesperson Lieutenant General Maly Socheata stated that Thailand unilaterally closed the border, and thus the responsibility to reopen it lies solely with the Thai side. The ministry warned citizens to verify information carefully before sharing.
title: Cambodia Rejects Claims of Request to Reopen Border for Emergency Goods

summary: Interior Minister Sar Sokha urged Cambodians to maintain socio-economic activities during the Khmer New Year despite ongoing border tensions with Thailand. Quoting Hun Sen, he emphasized that the nation should not be paralyzed by external pressures or "aggressive border encroachments." He highlighted that frontline troops are defending sovereignty so that those behind the lines can continue their daily lives and keep the economy moving.
title: Cambodia must remain resilient despite border strain, says Interior Minister

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence has officially denied social media reports and Thai media claims that it requested the reopening of the border for emergency goods. A ministry spokesman labeled the information 'false and misleading,' clarifying that Thailand made the unilateral decision to close the border and therefore holds the responsibility for reopening it.
title: Cambodia rejects 'false claims' of request to reopen Thai border

summary: Spokespersons for Senate President Hun Sen have rejected Thai media reports claiming he admitted that leaking an audio clip of a conversation with former Thai PM Paetongtarn Shinawatra was a mistake. Cambodian officials also dismissed rumors that they are seeking a reset in ties or begging for border gates to be reopened. The Cambodian side maintains that since Thailand was the one to close the gates, they must be the one to initiate the reopening.
title: Cambodia denies reports Hun Sen regretted leaked call clip, says it is not urging Thailand to reopen border checkpoints

summary: Thai authorities in Trat and Chanthaburi maintain a closure of key border crossings with no timeline for reopening. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed it is not yet the right time for discussions. Security has been reinforced with Royal Thai Navy units placed on high readiness to 'protect national sovereignty' along what they call the crucial frontline. Speculation about using these gates for humanitarian aid to Cambodia was also dismissed.
title: Thailand keeps Cambodia border crossings shut

summary: The Royal Thai Navy chief, Admiral Pairot Fuangchan, confirmed on April 16 that border crossings with Cambodia in Chanthaburi and Trat will remain closed. This follows reports that Hun Sen, President of the Cambodian Senate, had attempted to negotiate a reopening through a close aide. The Thai Navy stated they are strictly following government orders and will not reopen the checkpoints under any circumstances for now, citing national security as the core concern. The Navy has also moved to tighten internal security to prevent information leaks regarding military operations along the border.
title: Thai navy chief vows Cambodian border crossings will stay shut

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow stated that while Thailand is open to dialogue regarding border disputes, it will not be pressured into premature talks. He emphasized that negotiations cannot be dictated unilaterally by Cambodia setting dates without coordination. Thailand maintains that formal talks should wait until its internal political processes and the formation of a new government are complete.
title: Thailand says ready for talks with Cambodia, rejects 'pressure tactics'

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow claimed Thailand is ready for bilateral talks with Cambodia but criticized Prime Minister Hun Manet’s calls for negotiations as a form of pressure. While Cambodia has expressed a shift in focus toward bilateral dialogue to resolve border issues, Thailand maintains that it will not be forced to the table on a date set solely by Cambodia. The report notes that while there is talk of willingness, no concrete diplomatic actions have been taken to move forward, leaving the situation at a stalemate.
title: Stalled diplomacy? Despite Thai 'willingness' for bilateral negotiations, no action taken

summary: Thailand shows no signs of reopening border checkpoints closed since June 2025 due to security concerns. Security agencies expect the border to remain shut for the rest of 2026, citing ongoing military reinforcements by Cambodia and domestic political pressure.
title: Thai stance hardens as Cambodia border closure drags into 10th month

summary: Both Cambodian and Thai officials have dismissed rumors of active border negotiations. Thai Navy Commander Pairoj Fuangchan stated that border checkpoints remain closed and no formal request has been made to reopen them. Meanwhile, Cambodian Senate President Hun Sen emphasized that Cambodia has enough domestic supplies to withstand the closures and suggested focusing on local production instead of relying on cross-border trade.
title: Cambodia, Thailand deny reports of border negotiations

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that Prime Minister Hun Manet is focused on protecting national sovereignty. During the Khmer New Year, the government protested against what it calls Thailand's illegal occupation of heritage sites like the Tamone Thom and Ta Krabei temples. They also denied rumors that Cambodia is begging Thailand to reopen the border for cargo.
title: Gov't reaffirms border stance, rejects misinformation amid New Year

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest on April 19 regarding Thai military activities on April 18. Cambodia accuses Thai forces of consolidating illegal occupations in Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, and Pursat provinces. Specific actions cited include building an observation post near Preah Vihear Temple, constructing roads and bunkers in Oddar Meanchey, and land-clearing with heavy machinery in Pursat. Cambodia maintains these actions violate sovereignty and international law.
title: Cambodia Lodges Formal Protest Over Thai Military Activities Along Border

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a press release on April 19 regarding Thai military activities deep inside Cambodian territory. The statement highlighted the installation of razor wire and shipping container barricades. Cambodia remains committed to resolving the dispute through peaceful negotiations but insists that borderlines must not be changed by force, urging Thailand to de-escalate to preserve 'good neighbourliness'.
title: Formal protest against Thai border encroachments, Cambodia warns of sovereignty violations

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that Cambodia is closely monitoring Thai military activities in areas allegedly occupied illegally since December 2025 in Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, and Pursat. He clarified that recent Thai activities involve building bunkers and roads on ground they already held since the December 27, 2025 ceasefire, rather than new territorial advances. The formal protests serve as legal evidence for international dispute resolution and as a warning that Cambodia remains the true owner of the land.
title: Government continues to monitor Thai forces illegally occupying Khmer territory

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest against Thai armed forces for constructing observation posts, bunkers, and roads in disputed areas of Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, and Pursat provinces on April 18. Cambodia claims these actions violate its sovereignty and international agreements like the ASEAN Charter. The government emphasized it does not recognize any unilateral boundary claims by Thailand and called for a halt to these activities to maintain peace.
title: Cambodia lodges formal protest over Thai military activities along border

summary: Bilateral trade between Cambodia and Thailand reached nearly $700 million in the first quarter of 2026, though this represents a nearly 40% decrease compared to 2025. Economists note that while the land border is closed, goods are being rerouted through Laos or by sea. Aggressive military actions by Thai forces have led to a growing 'boycott Thai products' trend among Cambodian consumers, favoring domestic goods and imports from other nations.
title: Despite boycotts, Cambodia imported over $500 million of Thai goods in Q1

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona announced that Prime Minister Hun Manet is seeking to resume Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) talks. While both sides are reportedly adhering to a ceasefire, Cambodia is concerned about recent Thai military presence in cultural sites like Ta Moan Thom. Meanwhile, Senate President Hun Sen has called for a boycott of Thai goods to curb smuggling and support local production while the land border remains officially closed.
title: Phnom Penh presses Bangkok for border talks

summary: The Thai Defence Minister is calling for an investigation after a Thai national flag went missing from a flagpole in Chanthaburi province, near the Cambodian border. While some suspect Cambodian soldiers crossed over to remove it, Cambodian military commanders have 'firmly confirmed' they were not involved. Thai officials are trying to determine if it was an act of provocation or simply caused by strong winds.
title: Thai defence chief urges probe into missing border flag

summary: Cambodian authorities are officially protesting against what they call the 'illegal occupation' and consolidation of border areas by the Thai military. Photos shared in local media show shipping containers and barbed wire fences being set up by Thai forces in Pursat province. The Cambodian government also dismissed claims from Thai media suggesting a third armed conflict was imminent, calling those reports 'incorrect and baseless.'
title: Cambodia protests Thai consolidation of ‘illegal occupation’ in three border provinces

summary: Despite an ongoing boycott of Thai products and the closure of land borders, trade between Cambodia and Thailand reached $696 million in the first quarter. Due to the land checkpoints being shut, most trade has shifted to air and sea routes. Interestingly, trade with Vietnam has also seen a slight dip, showing that the regional economic situation remains fragile as the border conflict continues.
title: Tensions apart, Cambodia’s trade with Thailand reaches $696M

summary: The Thai-Cambodia Situation Joint Information Centre officially rejected Cambodia's accusations of encroachment. Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee stated that Thai forces are acting with caution and strictly adhering to the Joint Statement of the 3rd Special Meeting of the General Border Committee (GBC) from December 2025. Thailand claims there has been no troop movement or reinforcement and urged the use of direct communication to prevent misunderstandings.
title: Thailand rejects Cambodia border claim, cites legal framework

summary: The Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts issued a stern protest against Thai authorities for holding a religious ceremony at Ta Krabey Temple (known as Ta Kwai in Thailand) on April 22. Cambodia claims the site is within its sovereign territory and views the presence of the Thai Minister of Defence and Minister of Culture at the site as a serious violation of sovereignty and international law.
title: Cambodia Protests Thai Activities at Ta Krabey Temple

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that Cambodia is maintaining its economic growth and diplomatic goals despite ongoing territorial disputes with Thailand. While territorial integrity remains a top priority, the government is focusing on the 'Pentagonal Strategy' to reach high-income status by 2050, highlighting successful Khmer New Year celebrations as a sign of national resilience.
title: Border row fails to slow growth, diplomatic momentum

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts has repeated condemnations of Thailand escalating tensions along the border through creating a “fait accompli” at the Ta Krabei temple area. The ministry expressed deep concern over the presence of Thai authorities and armed forces in areas considered Cambodian sovereign territory.
title: Culture ministry: Thailand escalating border tensions through 'fait accompli' at Ta Krabei

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated that the ongoing tensions along the Cambodia-Thailand border should not cause despair among the population. He addressed concerns regarding Thai military reinforcements in areas allegedly seized in December 2025, including the construction of roads and trenches. He emphasized that the government is handling the situation to protect national sovereignty.
title: Government Spokesperson: Border issues will not discourage the people

source: Asia News Network / Phnom Penh Post
summary: At a seminar in Phnom Penh, experts discussed the impact of the May 28 soldier fatality which reignited border tensions. Researchers noted that the death of a Cambodian soldier has damaged bilateral trade and led to military build-ups fueled by nationalism. The discussion highlighted Cambodia's 'growing confidence' in its strategic partnerships, including with China, as a factor in the current standoff.
title: Scholars call for peaceful resolution to Cambodia-Thailand border dispute

source: Thai PBS World (covering Cambodian Ministry statement)
summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts has formally protested Thailand's hosting of a religious ceremony at the Ta Kwai Temple ruins. Cambodia claims the site is within its sovereign territory and views the high-level attendance of Thai Defense and Culture ministers as a 'serious violation' and an attempt to create a fait accompli on the ground.
title: Phnom Penh slams Thai ministers’ presence at Ta Kwai Temple rites

summary: Military delegates from Cambodia's Region 4 and Thailand's Region 2 held an informal meeting of the Regional Border Committee (RBC) secretariat at the Choam-Sa Ngam International Border Gate. The discussion focused on implementing the joint declarations from the 2025 border committee meetings and maintaining local coordination. The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense emphasized its commitment to peaceful resolution in accordance with international law and existing treaties.
title: Cambodia Region 4 and Thai Region 2 military hold informal meeting at Choam-Sa Ngam border

summary: Cambodia’s Ministry of Culture has strongly condemned a Buddhist ceremony held by Thai officials and military personnel at the Ta Krabey temple (known as Ta Kwai in Thailand). The temple was a flashpoint for deadly border clashes in 2025. Cambodia described the presence of high-level Thai ministers at the site as 'unlawful' and an attempt to reinforce illegal control over Cambodian territory, undermining peace negotiations.
title: Thailand ceremony at disputed border temple draws Cambodia rebuke

summary: Cambodian officials at the UN have formally rejected Thai accusations that Cambodia is a regional hub for online scams. The Cambodian delegation claimed Thailand is using this 'scam narrative' to deflect international attention from its own military incursions into Cambodian territory. They cited deadly clashes from 2025 that reportedly left over 100 dead and emphasized that Cambodia's actions have been in self-defense against Thai aggression.
title: Cambodia rejects Thai claims at UN, says 'scam narrative' used to justify border aggression

summary: The new Thai government under PM Anutin Charnvirakul plans to abolish the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand. Thai officials stated the move is due to a lack of progress over many years. Cambodia has previously warned that such a unilateral withdrawal would violate international law and the spirit of cooperation between the two nations.
title: Thailand set to scrap maritime dispute MOU with Cambodia

summary: In an informal meeting on Thursday, officials from the Secretariat of the Cambodia-Thailand Regional Border Committee met to coordinate local peace efforts. The discussion focused on implementing existing border peace agreements and strengthening local coordination between the two militaries to maintain stability on the ground.
title: Cambodian and Thai military officials hold border peace talks

summary: At the UN ECOSOC Forum, Cambodia's Deputy Secretary General Chou Heng stated that border conflict initiated by Thailand since 2025 has caused over 100 deaths and displaced 650,000 civilians. He noted that 48 schools and 22 health facilities remain closed. While a ceasefire has been in effect since December 27, 2025, sporadic incidents continue to hinder Cambodia's development and recovery efforts.
title: Cambodia Condemns Thai Aggression at UN Forum, Reports Over 100 Deaths and Massive Displacement

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi expressed hope for improved relations between Thailand and Cambodia during talks in Bangkok with Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul. Tensions have remained high following two rounds of armed border clashes last year. China reiterated its support for peaceful dialogue and regional stability, while also focusing on joint efforts to combat cyber scams.
title: China urges better Thailand-Cambodia relations

summary: Following heavy fighting along the Thai border in 2025, the Cambodian government is preparing a new conscription law targeting men aged 18 to 25. The move is framed as a patriotic duty to defend the motherland and national development, reflecting the high tensions that persist despite the current ceasefire.
title: Cambodia readies new conscription law for men aged 18-25

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed 'deep regret' following reports that Thailand intends to unilaterally withdraw from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding regarding overlapping maritime claims. A spokesperson stated on April 24 that this move undermines the cooperative spirit intended for joint resource exploitation in the Overlapping Claim Area (OCA).
title: Cambodia voices deep regret over Thailand's move to exit 2001 maritime MOU

summary: Australia has pledged AUD 1.5 million (approx. $1.08 million USD) to help Cambodia clear landmines and unexploded ordnance (UXO). The funding specifically targets border provinces littered with explosives left from the 2025 border conflict with Thailand. Ly Thuch of CMAA stated the aid will address humanitarian needs in communities facing high risk from recent contamination.
title: Australia Donates $1.08M to support Cambodia's mine clearing in conflict zones

summary: Pailin provincial authorities officially rejected social media reports claiming that Thai forces had secretly encroached on Cambodian territory in the province. Officials labeled the news as 'fake and baseless,' spread by opposition groups to cause confusion, and assured citizens that Cambodian troops are firmly guarding the border.
title: Pailin authorities deny rumors of Thai encroachment

summary: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra thanked citizens for their trust in Prime Minister Hun Manet’s leadership regarding the border conflict. He alleged that Thailand used unilateral maps instead of internationally recognized French colonial maps to seize land. He stated that Cambodian forces have fought to protect territorial integrity and the government will never abandon its right to reclaim land currently under 'illegal' Thai military occupation.
title: Information Minister thanks Cambodians for trusting government to solve border issues with Thailand

summary: Following Thailand's move to potentially revoke MOU44, Cambodia is highlighting its recent ratification of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) as a primary legal tool to protect its maritime rights. Information Minister Neth Pheaktra stated that UNCLOS provides a comprehensive basis for managing maritime claims and resources amidst the growing uncertainty over bilateral negotiations.
title: Cambodia turns to UNCLOS as legal shield as Thailand rethinks maritime pact

summary: Minister of Economy and Finance Aun Pornmoniroth projected 5% economic growth for 2026, a slight decrease from 5.2% in 2025. He cited external shocks and the impact of the ongoing border issue with Thailand as key challenges. The conflict has forced the government to redirect resources toward defense and humanitarian aid while trade with Thailand has reportedly declined by nearly 40% in early 2026.
title: Cambodia's economy expected to grow by 5% despite external shocks and border issue

summary: Cambodia has officially criticized Thailand at a UN forum for what it calls military aggression and the blocking of access by Thai forces in border areas. Officials report that over 34,000 people remain displaced due to these actions and the presence of unexploded ordnance from conflict last year. Thailand responded by accusing Cambodia of unprovoked attacks along the border in 2025.
title: Cambodia reproaches Thailand over military aggression

summary: Official state media reports that Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn met Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow on the sidelines of the ASEAN-EU meeting. Both sides emphasized full implementation of the Joint Statement from December 27, 2025, to maintain peace. Sokhonn stressed that lasting stability requires genuine respect for international law and existing treaties, aiming for regional harmony within ASEAN.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Reaffirm Commitment to Ceasefire

summary: Cambodia's Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn met with Thai counterpart Sihasak Phuangketkeow on the sidelines of an ASEAN-EU meeting in Brunei on April 27. The two held candid discussions on border tensions following the December 2025 ceasefire. Sokhonn emphasized that lasting peace requires full respect for international law and existing treaties. The meeting occurred amid reports that Thailand is considering revoking MoU 44 regarding maritime claims, though Thai officials stated such a move would not end bilateral negotiations.
title: Cambodian, Thai FMs discuss border issue in Brunei

summary: The Ministry of National Defence organized a visit for the Military Attachés Corps in Phnom Penh (MACPP) to the Ou Phluk Damrei area in Pursat province. Spokeswoman Maly Socheata stated that this second annual tour for 2026 aims to monitor the ceasefire situation along the Cambodian-Thai border and ensure transparency. The government reaffirmed its commitment to the peace agreements signed last October and December following recent conflicts.
title: Cambodia facilitates military attachés visit to border provinces following ceasefire

summary: A delegation from the Military Attachés Corps in Phnom Penh (MACPP) visited the Chey Chumneas Border Checkpoint in Pursat province on April 28. According to the Cambodian Ministry of National Defence, the visit allowed foreign representatives to observe areas where Thai forces have allegedly occupied territory and blocked access using shipping containers and barbed wire. The tour aimed to promote transparency regarding the border situation and monitor the implementation of the December 2025 ceasefire agreement.
title: Foreign Military Attachés Witness Thai Blockade at Cambodia Border Crossing

summary: Cambodian scholars and media professionals participated in the second China-Cambodia-Thailand Track II Dialogue in Beijing on April 20-21, 2026. The delegation reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to resolving border differences through mutual respect and dialogue. They promoted the 'Fuxian Consensus' as a roadmap to rebuild trust between Phnom Penh and Bangkok, moving from a zone of tension to a corridor of friendship and trade.
title: Cambodian delegation hails Fuxian Consensus at Beijing track II dialogue

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence reported that Thai military forces fired weapons on five occasions near the O'Smach border checkpoint in Oddar Meanchey province. This allegedly happened while the Military Attaché Corps Phnom Penh (MACPP), a group of foreign military representatives, was conducting an official observation visit. According to Lieutenant General Maly Socheata, nine rounds from M79 launchers and M16 rifles were fired between 10:35 am and 11:09 am on April 29, despite a ceasefire agreement being in place.
title: Thai troops fired during foreign military attachés' border visit, says Defence Ministry

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to strictly protecting the Cambodia-Thailand border. He stated that the government continues to defend territorial integrity based on international law, the Franco-Siamese treaties, and historical maps. He emphasized that Cambodia does not recognize any border changes resulting from the use of force. Bona noted that on April 28, the Ministry of National Defense facilitated a visit by foreign military attaches to observe areas in Pursat province currently occupied by Thai troops.
title: Government Spokesperson Reaffirms Cambodia's Firm Stance on Border Protection

summary: Foreign Ministers Prak Sokhonn and Sihasak Phuangketkeow held high-level talks on April 27 in Brunei to address simmering border tensions. The meeting follows Cambodian protests over alleged Thai airspace and land violations, as well as Bangkok's move to revoke the MoU 44 maritime agreement. Cambodia reported that Thai forces have blocked off areas in Pursat province with shipping containers and barbed wire, while illegally occupying six villages in Banteay Meanchey. Despite the friction, both nations reaffirmed their commitment to a December ceasefire.
title: Cambodia and Thailand meet for 'candid' discussion on border dispute

summary: Officials from Cambodia and Thailand met in Brunei to discuss a roadmap for restoring trust. Both sides expressed commitment to the existing ceasefire agreement. Cambodia expressed regret over Thai media reports suggesting a withdrawal from the 2001 maritime MoU.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Agree to Consider a Roadmap for Restoring Bilateral Relations

summary: Following a meeting with Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in Brunei, Prak Sokhonn clarified that Cambodia's vocal protests are necessary to protect national sovereignty. He alleged that Thai forces continue to occupy areas and use razor wire barricades to separate villages, which violates the Joint Statement of the 3rd Special GBC Meeting. He emphasized that the 'easy way' to silence Cambodia's complaints is for the Thai military to end its occupation.
title: Sokhonn: ‘As long as the Thai military stops illegal acts against us, that will be the end of it’

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn stated that Cambodia will only stop criticizing Thailand if the Thai military ceases its 'illegal activities' and occupation of Cambodian territory. He addressed reports from Thai media suggesting his rhetoric was damaging relations, countering that Thai forces have used shipping containers to block villages and prevent residents from returning home despite the December 27, 2025, ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia Reiterates Position on Ceasefire Implementation, Cites Ongoing Illegal Thai Occupation
